name: Xiomara Castro
summary: Castro advocates democratic socialism, stronger public services, taxation of privileged economic groups and national control of strategic resources. Her government combined social and environmental initiatives with emergency security powers and militarized prison management; her reproductive-rights agenda includes limited abortion exceptions and a contested sex-education record.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Her platform promises free, universally accessible public healthcare.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Her program requires state correction of market distortions.

public-ownership.rationale: She explicitly defends restoring state energy and infrastructure enterprises.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: She demands ending exemptions for the richest groups and a progressive tax system.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Her tax proposal subjects privileged companies to stronger controls and review.

cut-welfare.rationale: She defends major increases in poverty-reduction programs and public provision.

empower-police-military.rationale: She expands military prison control and directs armed anti-gang interventions.

abortion-legal.rationale: Her proposal allows abortion only for rape, serious fetal anomaly or danger to the pregnant woman’s life.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: She requests an autonomous UN-supported commission with corruption-investigation powers.

free-trade.rationale: She condemns imposed trade agreements for undermining sovereignty and domestic producers.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: She demands urgent economic and ecological transformation to prevent climate catastrophe.

state-directs-investment.rationale: She explicitly directs investment toward strategic, environmentally compatible production.

direct-votes.rationale: She demands deeper democracy through popular consultations.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: She pledges territorial titles and Indigenous governance.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Her platform identifies patriarchy as excluding women politically.

separated-powers.rationale: She promises restoring separation of the three state powers.

priority-to-poor.rationale: She prioritizes expanded social budgets and free electricity for the poorest households.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Her emergency policy suspends constitutional protections and expands detention powers.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: She promotes regional customs integration and coordinated Central American policies.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: She pledged comprehensive sex education, then vetoed a bill demanding greater parental input and redesign.

minority-language-support.rationale: She promises bilingual, culturally appropriate Indigenous education.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: She proposes converting tropical-forest countries’ entire foreign debt into environmental investment.

constituent-assembly.rationale: She proposes a directly elected constitution-making assembly.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: She demands financial compensation from countries responsible for historical warming.

ban-cartels.rationale: Her platform explicitly rejects monopolies and oligopolies.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Her platform demands parity throughout political participation.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: She condemns uncontrolled overconsumption and demands reductions in wealthy economies.

corporate-influence.rationale: She denounces multinational power over national decision-making and investment arbitration.

public-access-to-information.rationale: She celebrates repealing the secrecy law as an anticorruption measure.

national-law-over-international.rationale: She rejects investor arbitration that places private interests above national sovereignty.

participatory-democracy.rationale: She explicitly calls for effective, direct popular participation.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: She proposes an inclusive gender-identity law.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: She condemns international lenders’ conditional fiscal prescriptions as deepening dependency.

online-participation.rationale: She proposes digital participation in municipal policy decisions.

open-government-data.rationale: She proposes public legislative drafts, amendments and official agendas.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: She says ten wealthy families seek to capture democracy.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: She backs a new 20,000-person detention center and expanded enforcement.

recognise-genocide.rationale: She publicly recognizes and condemns the destruction in Gaza as genocide.

local-essentials-public.rationale: She rejects privatizing water, electricity, education and health services.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: She elevated the women’s institute into a cabinet-level ministry.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: She proposes autonomous Indigenous and Afro-descendant zones.

close-ties-china.rationale: She instructed diplomatic engagement with Beijing and sought wider partnerships beyond traditional allies.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Her electricity subsidy explicitly targets the poorest, alongside universal school meals.

no-business-privileges.rationale: She targets special tax privileges granted to connected corporate groups.

national-resource-control.rationale: She opposes transferring national resources and territory to multinational enclaves.

notes: No inferred answers. Full platform and 2024 address downloaded and searched; all themes and remaining nulls reviewed. Most recent enacted emergency-security policy supersedes earlier demilitarization proposals. Her three abortion exceptions do not support legalization in most cases. Contraception legalization is distinguished from abortion policy. Sex education is mixed because of the 2023 veto. No same-sex-marriage position is inferred from general LGBT protections. Investor arbitration opposition is limited evidence, not a claimed rejection of every international court. Primary speech statistics are treated as her claims, not independently verified outcomes. Home-values language does not establish the family-foundation proposition; trafficking enforcement does not establish adult recreational-drug policy; distributing public land does not establish expropriating large private estates.
